report.summary: Reviewed transport.py chunk 1/1: all docstring claims kept; observations on lock scope, error propagation, and sink protocol conformance.
risks: JsonlTransportSink.__init__ | low | asyncio.Lock is created at construction time, not at event-loop runtime; if the sink is constructed outside a running loop, the lock may bind to the wrong loop when publish is called in a different loop (e.g., multiple tests with fresh loops). | Verify whether the sink is ever constructed before a loop is running and then used in a different loop; if so, move lock creation into publish or use a per-call lock.

CompositeTransportSink.publish | low | Failures in later sinks propagate immediately, so earlier sinks may have published while later ones did not; the docstring says failures remain visible but not that partial fan-out is atomic. This may be acceptable but should be confirmed. | Check if any caller assumes all-or-nothing fan-out; if so, consider catching and aggregating exceptions.

JsonlTransportSink.publish | medium | The lock only serializes the file append, but the directory mkdir and file open are inside the lock; however, the lock is not held across the entire write? Actually it is: mkdir and open are inside the async with block. The risk is that the lock is created in __init__, which may be before the event loop, but the lock's loop is bound at first use. This is a potential cross-loop issue. | Confirm the sink is always constructed within the same loop that publishes; if not, document or fix.

JsonlTransportSink.publish | medium | The write uses the blocking `open` and `write` inside an async function. For large records or slow disks, this blocks the event loop. The lock does not mitigate blocking I/O. | Check if the sink is used in high-throughput or latency-sensitive contexts; if so, consider `asyncio.to_thread` or aiofiles.

handoff.purpose: Defines transport sink protocol and three sink implementations (in-memory, JSONL journal, composite fan-out).

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that appends records to an in-memory list.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink.records
symbols.note: List of TransportRecord instances; public attribute for inspection.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Async method that appends a record to self.records.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that appends JSON lines to a file with an asyncio lock.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Writes a JSON line to the file, creating parent directories as needed.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that fans out to multiple sinks sequentially.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink.sinks
symbols.note: Tuple of sinks to publish to.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Await sink.publish for each sink in order; exceptions propagate.

claims.text: Persist or forward one lossless transport record.
claims.why: The protocol only declares the method; implementations in this chunk either persist (Jsonl) or forward (Composite) without loss. InMemory retains the object.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The sink simply appends to a list in order; deterministic and minimal.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: publish serializes the record and appends a line to the file in append mode ('a'), preserving all records. No truncation or overwrite.

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: The loop awaits each sink.publish without catching exceptions, so failures propagate and are visible to the caller.

observations.what: The asyncio.Lock is created in __init__, not lazily; if the sink is constructed outside an event loop and then used in a different loop, the lock may be bound to the wrong loop.
The JSONL write uses blocking file I/O inside an async function, which can block the event loop for large records or slow disks.

CompositeTransportSink.publish does not handle exceptions per-sink, so a failure in a later sink prevents subsequent sinks from receiving the record; the docstring does not promise all-or-nothing, but this partial delivery may be unintended.
The protocol TransportSink is structural; the concrete sinks implicitly satisfy it. No runtime check enforces that a sink passed to CompositeTransportSink actually has an async publish method.
